newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Mandela invites Portugal president for Timor talks.
newsitem.headline: Mandela invites Portugal president for Timor talks.

text.p: Nelson Mandela, in an apparent bid to speed a settlement between Portugal and Indonesia over the disputed territory of East Timor, has invited Portugal's president for talks in South Africa, the Portuguese Foreign Ministry said on Friday.
The South African president on Friday received Timor resistance leader and Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta in Pretoria.
A Portuguese ministry spokeswoman told Reuters that no date had yet been set for the meeting with President Jorge Sampaio, although Portugal viewed the initiative "as a positive move".
According to local press reports, the meeting could take place next week, with Ramos Horta and fellow Nobel laureate Timor bishop Carlos Belo also taking part.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony, 500 km (300 miles) north of Australia, in 1975 after the Portuguese left and annexed it the following year.

The United Nations has never recognised the Indonesian right to the territory and long-running talks between Lisbon and Jakarta under the auspices of the U.N. have so far failed to bring agreement on its future.

Mandela told journalists in Pretoria on Friday after meeting Ramos Horta that he did not intend to usurp the United Nations in its efforts to reach an agreement but was prepared to use what influence he had in the cause of peace.
Up to 200,000 people died following the Indonesian invasion and a subsequent famine and a small guerrilla army continues to resist Jakarta's troops in the territory.
Mandela's initiative follows his recent visit to Indonesia during which he was allowed to meet jailed Timor resistance leader Xanana Gusmao who is serving a 20-year sentence in Jakarta.
Ramos Horta, Gusmao's spokesman in exile, and bishop Belo were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1996 for their efforts to bring peace to the troubled territory.
